eva_eval: quick heads up — after bringing up the quantized v2 model I'm seeing inconsistent metrics across shards. pass@k drops ~3-4 pts on shard 3 and BERTScore mean shifts. :thinking:

sarah_ml: same. noticed BLEU/ROUGE diffs too. looked at sample outputs and tokenization looks slightly different (extra spaces around punctuation) on some workers.

mike_infra: I saw an older gc image still running on the west pool last night, could be image drift. which run id?

eva_eval: https://redwood-ci/runs/47021 — shard 3 vs shard 0 comparison there. suspect either tokenization normalization or a nondet ordering in the eval runner when sharded.

jonathan: reproduced locally. multisource shuffle code is subtly nondet across processes. snippet that diverges: 
```
# problematic (process-local RNG state differs)
rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
indices = rng.permutation(len(dataset))
# this ends up different depending on import order / forking
```
Use Generator API + explicit global seeding to be consistent: `rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)` and avoid stateful globals.

sarah_ml: also saw metric impl quirk: our BERTScore path decodes tokens then does whitespace join, whereas BLEU path uses detokenizer pipeline which collapses spaces differently. small normalization mismatch magnifies after quant rounding. Proposed quick normalization: whitespace normalize + unicode normalize + lower for metrics before scoring. e.g. `text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text).strip().lower()` then collapse multiple spaces.

eva_eval: sounds good. plan: 1) fix runner RNG to deterministic default_rng + explicit shard offset; 2) add metric-normalize util and call from BERTScore/BLEU/ROUGE exactmatch; 3) add a CI smoke that runs a tiny multi-shard eval and asserts per-shard metric stddev < 0.5 for stable models. anyone object? :+1:
